company.name: Coventor, Inc., A Lam Research Company

positions.title: Graduate Student Researcher and Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
The role of being a graduate student was split into both researching and teaching. 

As a researcher:

-Performed large parallel simulations of small molecule dynamics on an 8-node Linux-based cluster and a Cray XE6m-200 supercomputer 
-Learned the robust, high-level physics of the project, including bond structure of the molecule, interaction strengths, substrate qualities, plane-wave basis wavefunction expansions and cutoff energies, k-point sampling, and more
-Prepared detailed input files and batch submission files (in Bash) in both ab initio and molecular-mechanics-based software
-Built parallel executables via PGI compilation
-Data parsing was performed directly in the Linux environment and in Open Office. Post-processing was done in MATLAB and visualization was primarily performed in XCrysDen and VMD. Trajectories of several nanoseconds were performed at various temperatures within the molecule's thermal stability region.
-Presented research at the American Physical Society March Meeting 2016 in Baltimore and prepared an in-depth thesis and presentation summarizing the project

As a teaching assistant:

-Taught the lab sections for six classes at UNH. The classes were both introductory and honors physics for scientist and engineers (calculus-based), and the biology-based physics class
-Duties included teaching lab sections, holding weekly office hours and review sessions before tests, and preparing material for a lecture at the beginning of lab
-Received excellent teaching evaluations every semester I taught
-In addition to teaching, I tutored several students in both high school and college-level physics, and second-semester calculus. All students that were tutored by me raised their grades from failing or C's to high B's or A's.

positions.title: Segre Intern
positions.description:
-Worked on improving the 20 experiments in the Advanced Experimentation Laboratory for the second-semester upper-division undergraduate lab class at UC Berkeley
-Thoroughly read through and understood each experiment and devised ideas to make the experiments better
-Streamlined lab manuals to be more concise and clear
-Repaired hardware including magnetic coils and optical setups
-Installed brand-new non-linear optics experiment housing and aligned/ calibrated new equipment with LabVIEW software including Fabry-Perot Interferometry calibration and optical resonance in a Rubidium gas sample for a diode laser
-Built several 24V power supplies for the undergraduate electronics lab class
-Duties all required close attention to detail and high level of creativity and thoughtfulness. Also required close attention to instruction from manager while simultaneously being self-starting and taking initiative to make lab experience better for future students

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description:
-Worked with a theoretical physics group who specialized in spacetime discretization for evolutionary systems
-Attended weekly meetings with my research adviser and learned upper-level physics and mathematics including Lagrangian mechanics and differential geometry
-Wrote small blocks of test code in C++ to test elements of large object-separated implementation of spacetime mesh being developed by my adviser
-Tasks of code included testing basic vector operations of given differential objects for proper behavior
-Constructed full report and summary on project upon completion
-Project provided me with experience in object-oriented programming in C++ and exposed me to upper-level math and physics concepts that would be useful later in my undergraduate and graduate careers
